summary.title: 4 - Designing a Simple Text Editor
summary.one_liner: You learn how to build a basic FLTK text editor in C++ with menus, file load/save, cut/copy/paste, find and replace, and syntax-style highlighting via a parallel style buffer.
takeaways: Structure a small FLTK application with an EditorWindow class, a menu bar built from Fl_Menu_Item arrays, and an Fl_Text_Editor backed by an Fl_Text_Buffer.
Implement file operations (load, save, save as, insert) and track unsaved changes with a modify callback that updates the window title.
Implement find, find again, replace, replace next and replace all using Fl_Text_Buffer search and edit methods.
Add syntax highlighting by pairing a style buffer with a style table and a style_update/style_parse routine that re-parses changed lines.
summary.summary: This FLTK documentation chapter walks through designing and writing a simple single-file text editor in C++. It covers the window and menu setup, the Fl_Text_Editor and Fl_Text_Buffer widgets, callbacks for file, edit and search operations, and a custom replace dialog. The final section introduces advanced syntax highlighting using a parallel style buffer, a style table, and a style_parse function that colors comments, strings, directives, types and keywords.
